name: Svelte 5 Runes
description: Enforces Svelte 5 runes-based reactivity, snippets, and fine-grained state management.
content:
# Svelte 5 Runes Rules

- Use `$state()` for reactive state instead of `let` declarations — runes make reactivity explicit and portable
- Use `$derived()` for computed values instead of `$:` reactive statements — derived values recalculate automatically
- Use `$effect()` for side effects instead of `$:` blocks — effects run after the DOM updates and clean up automatically
- Use `$props()` to declare component props — replaces `export let` and supports destructuring with defaults
- Use `$bindable()` for two-way bindable props — makes bind intent explicit in the component API
- Use Snippets (`{#snippet name()}...{/snippet}`) instead of slots — snippets are typed, composable, and can be passed as props
- Use `$state.raw()` for large objects that don't need deep reactivity — avoids proxy overhead
- Use `$effect.pre()` when you need to run logic before DOM updates — useful for scroll position preservation
- Use `$inspect()` during development to debug reactive values — it logs when values change
- Prefer `$derived.by()` for complex derivations that need multi-line logic or intermediate variables
- Extract shared reactive logic into `.svelte.ts` files — runes work outside components for reusable stores
- Use event attributes (`onclick`) instead of `on:click` directive — Svelte 5 uses standard DOM event naming
